questions.question: What causes the proximity effect in cardioid microphones? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• It is caused by the phase difference between the front and rear of the diaphragm in pressure-
  • gradient microphones (like cardioids). As the source gets closer, the low -frequency boost
  • increases.

  • signals common to both input leads (noise/interference) while passing the differential signal.

questions.question: Differentiate between line cable and speaker cable? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Line Cables- carry low-voltage, high-impedance signals. They are shielded to protect against
  • EMI/RFI interference- Speaker Cables- carry high-voltage, low-impedance signals. They are
  • unshielded and use thicker gauge wire to handle high current without significant power loss.

questions.question: Explain clipping distortion with a neat waveform diagram. How can it be minimized? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Occurs when an amplifier is pushed beyond its voltage limits, "cutting off" the peaks and
  • troughs of the waveform- The sine wave peaks become flattened, resembling a square wave-
  • Minimise by lowering input gain, using a limiter, or using an amplifier with higher headroom.

questions.solution_html:
• Operates on the principle of a variable capacitor - a thin diaphragm and a solid backplate act
  • as the two plates of a capacitor. Sound waves move the diaphragm, changing the capacitance
  • and creating an electrical signal. It requires phantom power (+48V).

questions.question: Discuss the advantages and limitations of OFC in audio communication? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Advantages:
  • - High bandwidth, low distortion
  • - Immune to electromagnetic interference
  • - Low signal loss, long-distance transmission
  • - Electrical isolation prevents ground loops
  • - Limitations:
  • - Higher cost
  • - Fragile, prone to breakage
  • - Requires special transmitters/receivers
  • - Difficult to repair/splice.

questions.question: Explain in detail the concept of loudspeaker baffles and enclosures. / [CO4] [12x2 = 24]
questions.solution_html:
• Baffles: A board used to mount drivers, preventing the rear sound wave (which is 180 degrees
  • out of phase) from cancelling the front wave. Enclosures include Sealed (Acoustic
  • Suspension) for tight bass, and Ported (Bass Reflex), which uses a tuned vent to increase
  • low-frequency efficiency.
